title: Phase Training
subtitle: Targeting timing relationships between oscillatory signals
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating phase training within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain phase training without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in phase training.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to phase training.

sections.explainSimply: Phase training attempts to alter the timing relationship between signals.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Phase estimates are highly sensitive to filtering, reference and volume conduction. Small processing changes can alter apparent lag.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Clinical claims about phase normalisation require transparent methods and independent replication.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Choosing a camera lens: every method emphasises some information and introduces its own distortions.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand phase training to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: A precise number can still be a fragile measurement.
sections.clinicalPearl: The trained metric is an intermediate target; the clinical endpoint is meaningful function.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using phase training predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: A precise number can still be a fragile measurement. Evidence classification: emerging; insufficient clinical evidence.
